title: Cord and Charger Organization: How to End the Tangle (and Find a Charger When You Need One)
description: Tangled cords, mystery cables and never a charger in sight? An easy cord and charger setup for busy brains, plus 8 Amazon finds to tame the tangle.
intro:
Somewhere in your home is a drawer, basket or bag full of cords. Some of them charge things you own. Some charge things you haven't owned since 2014. They are all tangled together.

And yet, when your phone is at 3%, there's never a charger where you are.

Cords are tricky for our brains because they're small, they all look alike and they wander. The fix is a few simple homes and some labels. Here's how to sort the tangle in small steps, plus eight Amazon finds that keep cords where you need them. With holiday gifts (and new gadgets) on the way, now's a good time.

sections.heading: Step 1: Dump and sort, three piles (15 minutes)
sections.body:
Gather every loose cord into one spot. Sort them into three piles:

- **Use it:** You know what it charges and you use it often.
- **Maybe:** You think it goes with something.
- **Mystery:** No idea.

Put the mystery pile in a bag and label it with today's date. If you don't need anything from it in three months, recycle it at an electronics drop-off.

sections.heading: Step 2: Label every cord you keep
sections.body:
This is the step that changes everything. Put a small label or colored tag on each end: "Phone," "Kindle," "Headphones." Once they're labeled, you'll never test five cords to find the right one again.

For families, give each person a cord color. Blue cords are Mom's. Nobody "borrows" by accident.

sections.heading: Step 3: Put chargers where you use them
sections.body:
Chargers wander because they live in one place and we need them in another. Instead, give each spot its own charger: one by your bed, one by the couch, one in the kitchen, one in your bag.

An extra charger or two costs less than the time we spend looking. And it means a charger never has to leave its spot.

sections.heading: Step 4: Make a family charging station
sections.body:
Pick one spot near the kitchen or entry, close to an outlet. Add a multi-port charging hub so phones, tablets and watches can charge together.

Make it the evening drop spot: phones go there at bedtime. It cuts down on lost phones in the morning, and on late-night scrolling too.

sections.heading: Step 5: Corral the extras
sections.body: Spare cords, earbuds and adapters go into one small organizer with pockets, or a box with dividers. Roll each cord loosely and close it with a strap so it doesn't tangle again. One bin, one spot, everyone knows where it is.

sections.heading: Step 6: Tame the cords behind the desk or TV
sections.body: A cord box hides a power strip and the extra length of cable. Adhesive cord clips along the edge of a desk or nightstand keep chargers from sliding to the floor every time you unplug. Two minutes to stick on, and you'll stop crawling under furniture.

outro:
Cord chaos isn't about being messy. It's a lot of small, look-alike things with no home. Labels, a charger in every spot and one bin for extras quiets the tangle for good.

If the junk drawer that holds all those cords needs help too, *The Messy Brain Home Reset* has a gentle plan for every catch-all spot in the house.
